holidays.name: National Cashew Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the curvy, buttery nut that is actually the seed of a fruit. Snack on them roasted, salted, or blended into creamy cashew cheese and sauces.
holidays.origin: One of many unofficial American food holidays on the calendar, promoted by food enthusiasts and snack makers. It is observed on November 23, with a second National Cashew Day sometimes marked on October 17.
holidays.funFact: Cashews grow on the bottom of a fruit called the cashew apple, and the shells contain a caustic oil related to poison ivy, which is why cashews are never sold in the shell.

holidays.name: Fibonacci Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the famous number sequence where each number is the sum of the two before it: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21... Math nerds eat spiral-shaped foods and spot patterns in pinecones and sunflowers.
holidays.origin: The date 11/23 reads as 1, 1, 2, 3, which are the first digits of the Fibonacci sequence. Math fans adopted it as an unofficial holiday honoring Leonardo of Pisa, known as Fibonacci.
holidays.funFact: Fibonacci introduced the Hindu-Arabic numeral system to Europe in his 1202 book Liber Abaci, and the sequence named after him was already known in Indian mathematics centuries earlier.

holidays.name: Doctor Who Anniversary Day
holidays.description: Fans of the time-traveling Time Lord celebrate the anniversary of the show's first broadcast with marathons, bow ties, scarves, and arguments over the best Doctor.
holidays.origin: Doctor Who premiered on the BBC on November 23, 1963, the day after President Kennedy was assassinated. The episode was rebroadcast the following week because of the disruption to many viewers.
holidays.funFact: Doctor Who is among the longest-running science fiction TV series in the world, and the show's 50th anniversary special in 2013 was simulcast in over 90 countries on the same day, November 23.

holidays.name: Espresso Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the small but mighty shot of concentrated coffee. Fans of the strong brew toast with tiny cups and buzz through the day with extra energy.
holidays.origin: A caffeine-fueled unofficial food and drink holiday celebrated by coffee lovers and cafes, who like to offer specials on espresso drinks on this date.
holidays.funFact: The first espresso machine patent was granted to Angelo Moriondo of Turin, Italy, in 1884, and despite the strong flavor, a shot of espresso contains less caffeine than a typical cup of drip coffee.

holidays.name: Turkey Pardoning Day Season Celebration
holidays.description: Around late November, the US President officially spares a lucky turkey from becoming dinner, treating the bird to a ceremony with jokes, press, and a retirement on a farm.
holidays.origin: The tradition is often traced to Abraham Lincoln pardoning a turkey named Jack for his son Tad, and President George H. W. Bush formalized the modern ceremony in 1989.
holidays.funFact: The pardoned turkeys are given official names such as Peas and Carrots, and some have lived out their days at places like Disneyland or university farms, though many only survive a short time because they are bred to grow fast.
